assertions.name: all_four_candidates_are_tied_by_every_letter_sum
assertions.source: all four have writhe +2 and length 2, so the crossing COUNT (the corpus's live cost in GammaGammaWordSelection) and the crossing ENERGY E_cross (a sum over letters) take one value across all four. LetterSumBlindness.letterSum_perm_invariant makes this structural rather than coincidental: no letter-sum, for any q and any coefficients, can do better

assertions.name: the_pair_kernel_separates_the_candidates_a_letter_sum_ties
assertions.source: 4 distinct proton values over 4 candidates, against ONE value for every letter-sum. So a separation-weighted pair kernel is a cost that can distinguish what the crossing count cannot -- which is the precondition the GammaGammaWordSelection cost socket needs and the crossing count fails. It does NOT follow that this cost should be adopted or minimised; that is a choice this probe does not make

assertions.name: the_separation_weight_is_what_breaks_the_tie_not_the_pairing
assertions.source: on the SHARP pair -- same letter multiset, same writhe, differing only in ORDER -- the weighted kernel separates by 0.91996925 against 0.0 unweighted. This is the measured form of ECatBlockDecomposition.pairSum_not_perm_invariant: pairing alone is not enough, because a kernel symmetric in its two letters and blind to their separation is permutation-invariant again. The 1/d_arc^2 factor of the O'Hara integrand is doing the work, and it is the factor the spec supplies rather than one chosen here

assertions.name: this_is_a_discretisation_and_not_E_cat
assertions.source: E_cat is a continuum double integral over S^1 x S^1 and has no producer in the corpus -- `energy : R` in CategoricalMobiusEnergy is a bare structure field. What is computed here is a discretisation whose three factors are read off prop:mobius-energy; whether its continuum limit is E_cat is UNPROVED, and the classical-limit leg it would need is assumed rather than derived and carries an unretired blindness incident (E_cat = 1 + const for every knot, no sorry). Recorded as an assertion so the boundary travels with the numbers

description: Implements the discretised E_cat double integral as a separation-weighted pair kernel over the braid word -- each factor read off prop:mobius-energy rather than chosen: the letter pair for D(g(s)) (x) D(g(t)), the Markov trace tr_M(w_i w_j) for lambda . tr_A, and 1/d_arc^2 for the measure factor, with d_arc the CYCLIC separation since a braid closure is a circle. Measures whether this cost separates the four two-crossing gluon candidates that every letter-sum provably ties, and contrasts it against the same sum with the separation weight removed -- the control for ECatBlockDecomposition.pairSum_not_perm_invariant. It is NOT E_cat (that is a continuum integral with no producer), it selects no word, and the per-block split is proved a refinement in Lean but not computed here.

kernel.d_arc: min(j-i, L-(j-i)) -- cyclic, because a braid closure is a circle
kernel.provenance: each factor read off prop:mobius-energy; no fitted constant, no chosen branch
